incidents.vector: Single operator using three npm maintainer aliases (mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, t-in-one) published packages across nine organizational scopes mimicking real internal corporate namespaces, including direct impersonation of Sberbank's SberPay payment widget; obfuscated postinstall stager downloaded a reconnaissance payload from oob.moika[.]tech.
incidents.impact: Two-phase supply-chain attack design: current 'reconnaissance-only' mode fingerprints environments and exfiltrates hostnames, env vars and developer context, with a server-side toggle to switch to full exploitation. Packages were removed after Microsoft notification to npm; no confirmed breach of Sberbank or other named impersonated targets.

incidents.victim: npm / AWS, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub Actions developer ecosystem
incidents.vector: Threat actor (alias 'vpmdhaj') published 14 typosquatted npm packages mimicking OpenSearch and ElasticSearch libraries that auto-executed credential-stealing payloads at install time, including a stealthier loader that abuses the legitimate Bun runtime to evade install-time C2 detection.
incidents.impact: Stolen AWS STS sessions, Secrets Manager material across 16+ regions, HashiCorp Vault tokens, npm publish tokens and GitHub Actions tokens — enabling cloud lateral movement and downstream supply-chain pivoting. Packages were removed by npm after Microsoft notification.

incidents.vector: Pseudonymous researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' publicly released six Windows zero-day vulnerabilities (BlueHammer, UnDefend, RedSun, YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma) with working proof-of-concept code on GitHub between April and May 2026, without coordinated disclosure to Microsoft.
incidents.impact: Microsoft confirmed BlueHammer, UnDefend and RedSun have been exploited in live intrusions and all three are now on CISA's KEV catalog. The three more recent vulnerabilities (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma) remain unpatched. The researcher has threatened additional releases on July 14 (Patch Tuesday).

incidents.victim: Education, transportation, healthcare and financial-sector organizations (multi-region)
incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service (tracked as Storm-2697) deploys a Go-based encryptor using per-file Curve25519/XChaCha20 keys, paired with aggressive self-propagation across mapped network drives, scheduled-task SYSTEM persistence, and PowerShell-based Defender disablement and log clearing.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed impact across organizations in North America, South America, Europe, Africa and Asia; double-extortion model with data exfiltration before encryption. The operators recently formed an official partnership with BreachForums to recruit affiliates, likely expanding activity.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud (Chinese-speaking, tracked as GHOST STADIUM)
incidents.vector: Pixel-perfect FIFA clone built using the Chinese Layui 2.7.6m UI library across 300+ active phishing domains (4,300+ registered since August 2025); the kit replicates FIFA's authentication flow, silently redirects victims to the real site to appear successful, and submits password-reset parameters to lock victims out so attackers can resell legitimate tickets.
incidents.impact: Group-IB estimates 47,400+ potential victims for premium and hospitality ticket fraud alone (priced $1,500-$10,000+), with losses on that tier projected at $71M-$474M and total losses across credential theft, ticket sales, counterfeit merchandise, streaming and gambling 'reasonably reach[ing] into the billions.'

incidents.victim: THE.Hosting / WorkTitans B.V. / MIRhosting (Russia-tied bulletproof hosting)
incidents.vector: Dutch fiscal crimes agency FIOD raids on May 18 seized 800+ servers and arrested two operators — Russian-born Andrey Nesterenko and a 57-year-old Amsterdam resident, Youssef Zinad — charged with sanctions evasion. The network is the latest rebrand of Stark Industries (sanctioned 2025), which moved AS44477 to PQ Hosting, then AS209847 under WorkTitans B.V.
incidents.impact: Servers seized in Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk; customer data on seized hardware reported lost. Threat-intelligence firm ELLIO reports scanning activity from THE.Hosting's IP space (geolocated across 12 countries) has continued at near-pre-raid levels, now also probing ICS protocols (DNP3, EtherNet/IP) and databases (MongoDB, Redis, PostgreSQL, Oracle).

incidents.vector: Former TD Bank employee Cheungkin (Kelvin) Lam, 28, of Queens, NY, accepted bribes to identify customer accounts with large balances and shared confidential customer information with outside co-conspirators; separately bribed an employee at a second financial institution to falsify bank records used to open accounts for fraud schemes.
incidents.impact: Lam received at least $155,000 in bribes and facilitated more than $3.4M in fraud losses across two financial institutions between January 2021 and August 2022. He pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit wire fraud affecting a financial institution and making false bank entries; faces up to 30 years in prison at October sentencing.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data brokerage to Jamaican scammers
incidents.vector: North Carolina lead-list broker Troy Murray, operating under the pseudonym 'Steve Dixon', sold lists of elderly Americans' names, phone numbers, addresses and email addresses to Jamaican lottery-fraud scammers from 2016 to 2023; payments were collected via wire transfer and (after wire blocks) pre-paid gift cards.
incidents.impact: Murray sent 22,000+ lead lists containing the personal information of more than 7 million elderly Americans and earned $5.2M; victim losses exceeded $9.5M. Sentenced May 28 to 121 months in prison plus $5.2M forfeiture for conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

incidents.victim: AI infrastructure built on the Starlette Python framework (LiteLLM, vLLM, MCP servers, AI proxies)
incidents.vector: X41 D-Sec disclosed CVE-2026-48710 ('BadHost') — a Host-header parsing flaw in the Starlette Python asynchronous web framework that lets attackers craft requests so the server treats private endpoints as public, bypassing authentication. Exploit example: GET /privateendpoint HTTP/1.1 with Host: example.com/public?bar=
incidents.impact: Starlette underpins a large portion of modern AI-server infrastructure including LiteLLM, vLLM, AI proxy servers, MCP servers and agent frameworks; patches were released but a significant portion of deployed AI backends are believed to remain unpatched. X41 published a scanner; no confirmed exploitation reported yet.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (ShinyHunters / Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters)
incidents.vector: Charter confirmed a security breach after its name was published on the ShinyHunters dark-web data-leak portal; ShinyHunters (Bling Libra) typically uses voice-phishing of help-desk staff to harvest SaaS credentials and intercept MFA codes.
incidents.impact: Specific data volume and customer impact not yet disclosed by Charter; ShinyHunters has a pattern of layering DDoS and media leaks on top of pure data-theft extortion when victims do not pay.

incidents.vector: Attackers used compromised credentials issued to other Lithuanian government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data to query the state registry.
incidents.impact: Approximately 600,000 records exfiltrated including property information, real names and cadastral details. Lithuania's state registry has confirmed the breach; entry-point credentials traced back to other government agencies.

incidents.victim: Independent Australian MP Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: Suspected foreign-state actor compromised the WhatsApp account of independent Australian MP Zali Steggall and three of her staff in March 2026, in what is believed to be part of a Russian campaign targeting foreign politicians' Signal and WhatsApp accounts.
incidents.impact: Scope of message and contact-list exposure not publicly detailed. Reporting attributes the activity to the same operational pattern of Russia-attributed messenger account hijacks seen against politicians in Europe; Australian authorities have not publicly confirmed attribution.

incidents.vector: Play ransomware group named MyPillow on its data-leak site and claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network; intrusion vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: MyPillow has not publicly confirmed the incident as of reporting. Play is one of the most prolific double-extortion crews of the past two years.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited CVE-2026-5426, a ViewState deserialization vulnerability stemming from hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values shared across KnowledgeDeliver deployments installed before Feb 24 2026; deployed BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) in-memory IIS web shell and modified application JavaScript to serve a fake 'security plugin' download.
incidents.impact: Targeted users were redirected to a fake installer leading to a Cobalt Strike BEACON infection; the payload was encrypted with a key derived from the victim organization's name, indicating targeted preparation. Mandiant collaborated with the vendor on remediation; customers should rotate machine keys.

incidents.victim: Japanese consumers (Apple, PayPay, Rakuten, JR, Nintendo, JCB and others)
incidents.vector: YY Lai Yu (YY来鱼) phishing-as-a-service platform delivers 400+ Japanese-language templates via RCS and iMessage (bypassing SMS carrier filters), with real-time admin panels that intercept one-time passcodes and lures themed around expiring loyalty points and the Japan Winter Electricity Subsidy.
incidents.impact: GTIG analysis of a dozen Chinese-language PhaaS offerings shows mature shift from credential harvesting to real-time MFA bypass and exploitation of digital-wallet provisioning to tokenize stolen cards for high-value transactions and ATM withdrawals; one platform (Darcula) attributed to UNC5814 uses AI-generated page clones to evade signature detection.

incidents.victim: Technology-sector professionals in the U.S., Israel and UAE
incidents.attacker: Iran — state-sponsored espionage (MOIS-linked, tracked as Screening Serpens / UNC1549)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing recruitment lures (fake job requisitions and a spoofed video-conferencing installer) deliver DLL-sideloading chains for six new RAT variants in two malware families (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2); .NET AppDomainManager hijacking disables application security via legitimate config files, and C2 traffic is split across 3-5 unique Azure-hosted domains per target.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 assesses with moderate-high confidence that Screening Serpens conducted coordinated espionage campaigns timed to the Middle East regional conflict that began Feb 28 2026; deployments observed against U.S., Israeli and UAE entities plus two additional Middle Eastern targets between February and April 2026.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access to the agency's code development platform created a public GitHub profile ('Private-CISA') in November 2025 and disabled GitHub's built-in protection against publishing secrets; the most sensitive credentials were posted in late April 2026.
incidents.impact: Plaintext AWS GovCloud keys and dozens of credentials to internal CISA systems exposed; an RSA private key giving access to a CISA-IT GitHub app with full read/write to every CISA repository was not invalidated until KrebsOnSecurity escalated. Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-NH) and Rep. Bennie Thompson (D-MS) sent formal letters demanding answers; CISA was still rotating keys more than a week after notification.

incidents.vector: Two Vietnamese government networks breached; intrusions initially went undetected and were only discovered after the breaches had occurred.
incidents.impact: The compromised networks store the data of millions of citizens; investigations are underway by Vietnamese authorities.

incidents.vector: Threat actors stole medical records and biometric data including fingerprints and palm prints; specific intrusion vector not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected; the breach is particularly sensitive because biometric identifiers such as fingerprints and palm prints cannot be reissued once stolen.

incidents.vector: 23-year-old Ottawa resident Jacob Butler operated the Kimwolf IoT botnet — enslaving devices traditionally firewalled from the internet such as digital photo frames and web cameras — and rented the botnet to other cybercriminals and used it for record-setting DDoS attacks.
incidents.impact: Kimwolf was tied to DDoS attacks measuring nearly 30 Tbps (record volume) and issued 25,000+ attack commands, including attacks that affected DoD IP address ranges; some victims reported losses exceeding $1M. Butler was arrested by Ontario Provincial Police on a U.S. extradition warrant and charged in both Canada and an Alaska district court.

incidents.vector: Unprotected Elasticsearch database left exposed on the public internet for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal details of nearly 19 million customers tied to their WeChat accounts (including phone numbers and full names) were exposed. The server was eventually secured.

incidents.vector: BlueSky accounts compromised since April 2026 and used to post pro-Kremlin, anti-Ukraine propaganda; activity attributed to the Russian disinformation group Matryoshka.
incidents.impact: BlueSky has been suspending affected accounts until owners can resecure them; campaigns are part of broader Russian influence operations also targeting Armenia, Moldova and Germany.

incidents.vector: GitHub employee installed the Nx Console VS Code extension, which had been compromised earlier in the TanStack/Mini Shai-Hulud supply-chain wave; the malicious extension exfiltrated GitHub credentials and internal repository data.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal GitHub code repositories were stolen and offered for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens. Grafana also linked its own intrusion days earlier to the same TanStack incident.

incidents.vector: Over 5,700 malicious commits pushed on May 18 injected GitHub Actions workflows containing credential-stealing payloads designed to harvest keys, tokens and other secrets from impacted repositories' CI/CD environments.
incidents.impact: More than 5,500 GitHub repositories infected; secrets, keys and tokens exposed to the campaign operators with risk of downstream supply-chain pivoting through stolen publishing credentials.

incidents.victim: TanStack, OpenSearch, UiPath, Mistral AI and 169+ npm packages (Mini Shai-Hulud)
incidents.vector: Attacker chained three GitHub Actions weaknesses against TanStack/router with no stolen credential required: a Pwn Request via a fork's pull_request_target workflow, poisoning of a 1.1 GB pnpm GitHub Actions cache, and extraction of an OIDC token from runner /proc memory which was POSTed directly to registry.npmjs.org.
incidents.impact: Within six minutes 84 malicious package artifacts were published across 42 @tanstack/* packages, with the self-propagating worm reaching 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages and PyPI by end of day — including @opensearch-project/opensearch, 57 @uipath/* packages and @mistralai/mistralai. Unit 42 estimates 520 million cumulative downloads in the affected window; this is the first documented case of a worm publishing npm packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance.
